Option C execution contradicts itself: its first sentence claims the weight sense is 'one a dictionary gives first' and the RETAGGED note that follows disowns that claim. Standard dictionaries give the moral-hesitation sense first, so the claim left on the note is false.

Option A 'He says her mum says a lot of things' is a literal, true account of what Grandad does with Priya's words at line 10, and the question 'What does Grandad do with what Priya tells him?' admits it. Its execution's 'rather than saying what he does' does not hold, because saying is what he does. The walk script also never reaches the key and ends on an irrelevant fact ('Line 10 says the bolt moves half a centimetre').

Option A's tag child hint ('Compare the parts column by column, starting with the tenths') tells the child to compare, and this question compares nothing. Option C's hint lists only whole-number columns ('Ones, tens, hundreds, thousands') for a tenths-versus-hundredths slip. Neither hint fits this item.

Option B's tag child hint ('Look at the words in the question. Are things getting bigger, smaller, or being shared?') does not fit a bare calculation: 'Work out 483 - 176.' has no words to read and the minus sign is given. A child who picked 659 is told something untrue of this item.
